items.followUp: Define electron affinity and state its general trend down a group.

rubric.why: The definition identifies the energy needed to remove an electron from a gaseous atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that energy is required to remove an electron from an isolated gaseous atom.

rubric.why: Ionization energy generally decreases down a group.
rubric.description: States the trend down a group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that ionization energy decreases down a group.

modelAnswer: Ionization energy is the energy required to remove the outermost electron from an isolated gaseous atom.
It generally decreases down a group because atomic size and shielding increase.

items.followUp: What type of bond is formed in a hydrogen molecule, and how many electron pairs are shared?

rubric.why: A nitrogen molecule contains a triple bond.
rubric.description: Identifies the bond as a triple bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the bond in nitrogen is a triple bond.

rubric.why: Each nitrogen atom shares three electrons with the other atom, forming the covalent bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that each nitrogen atom shares three electrons with the other.

modelAnswer: Each nitrogen atom shares three electrons with the other nitrogen atom.
The atoms form a triple covalent bond, written N≡N.

items.followUp: Why does a solution form a homogeneous mixture while a suspension does not?

rubric.why: Suspension particles do not dissolve uniformly in the medium.
rubric.description: Explains how the particles behave in a suspension.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the particles do not dissolve uniformly.

rubric.why: Uneven distribution or settling means the mixture is not uniform throughout.
rubric.description: Explains why a suspension is not homogeneous.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the particles are unevenly distributed or may settle.

modelAnswer: The particles of a suspension do not dissolve uniformly in the medium.
They are unevenly distributed and may settle, so the suspension is a heterogeneous, not homogeneous, mixture.

items.followUp: Why are noble gases generally unreactive?

rubric.why: Silver and gold have little tendency to lose electrons.
rubric.description: States their low tendency to lose electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that silver and gold have a low tendency to lose electrons.

rubric.why: Their low tendency to lose electrons explains why they do not readily react.
rubric.description: Links their electron behavior to their low reactivity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they do not readily react.

modelAnswer: Silver and gold have a low tendency to lose electrons.
Therefore, they do not readily react with other substances and are among the least reactive metals.

items.followUp: Write any five properties of cathode rays.

rubric.why: Canal rays are positively charged particles and consist of positive ions formed from the gas in the discharge tube.
rubric.description: States the charge and composition of canal rays.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for identifying canal rays as positively charged and as positive ions of the gas in the discharge tube.

rubric.why: Canal rays travel in straight lines and are deflected toward the negative plate in an electric field.
rubric.description: States their path and electric-field deflection.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for giving both properties: straight-line travel and deflection toward the negative plate.

accept: depends on the nature of the gas
rubric.why: The charge-to-mass ratio of canal-ray particles varies with the gas used.
rubric.description: States that their charge-to-mass ratio depends on the gas.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the charge-to-mass ratio depends on the nature of the gas.

modelAnswer: Canal rays are streams of positively charged particles.
They consist of positive ions formed from the gas in the discharge tube.
In an electric field, they are deflected toward the negative plate.
Their charge-to-mass ratio depends on the nature of the gas in the tube.
